newsitem.title: UK: Britain confident of peaceful Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Britain confident of peaceful Hong Kong handover.

text.p: The British government said on Tuesday it was confident next June's transfer of Hong Kong sovereignty to China would take place peacefully.

Deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine told a meeting of Commonwealth officials that the Commonwealth had "reaffirmed its interest in a successful transition for Hong Kong, and I am very confident that this will be achieved".
"China has too much to lose if Hong Kong's outstanding economic success does not continue," he added.
Hong Kong's six million people will leave the Commonwealth, a grouping made up mainly of Britain and its former colonies and protectorates, when it becomes part of China.
The Commonwealth officials are holding a two-day meeting in London to prepare the ground for a Commonwealth heads of government meeting next October in Edinburgh, Scotland.

Commonwealth officials said the issue of Nigeria would be discussed at the London meeting, but only in terms of whether it was complying with demands for democratic reforms. No fresh policy decisions would be taken this week.
Nigeria, which has a military government, was suspended from the Commonwealth in November 1995 after the execution of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other minority rights activists.

Commonwealth ministers also agreed a series of sanctions -- including a ban on sporting links and arms sales to Nigeria -- but suspended these while further talks were held. A ministerial action group agreed in New York in September to send a fact-finding mission to Nigeria and sanctions are still frozen.
